question: Mangalampalli Balamuralikrishna was an Indian Carnatic singer born in Sankaraguptam village of which state?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Andhra Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mangalampalli Balamuralikrishna was born in Sankaraguptam village, located in the state of **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• He was a renowned **Carnatic vocalist, composer, and multi-instrumentalist**, celebrated for his immense contributions to Indian classical music.
 
• Balamuralikrishna performed extensively across India and globally, earning critical acclaim for his unique style and technical mastery in Carnatic music.
 
• He received numerous awards during his lifetime, including the prestigious **Padma Vibhushan** in 1991 and the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award** in 1975.
 
• His birthplace, Sankaraguptam, is located in the **East Godavari district** of Andhra Pradesh, a region historically known for its rich cultural and musical heritage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carnatic Music:**

 
 
• Carnatic music is one of the two major classical music traditions of India, originating in South India.
 
• It is characterized by its highly structured compositions and emphasis on vocal music.
 
• Key elements include ragas (melodic frameworks) and talas (rhythmic patterns).
 
• Prominent composers in Carnatic music include Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, and Shyama Sastri.
 
 
 
• **Contribution to Music:**
 
 
• Balamuralikrishna composed several kritis (devotional songs), varnams, and tillanas in Carnatic music.
 
• He was known for popularizing rare ragas and experimenting with new ragas and talas.
 
• He played various instruments, including the viola, mridangam, and kanjira, showcasing his versatility.
